title: MRI during pregnancy
what: An MRI without radiation. It is done in pregnancy when an ultrasound does not give a full answer about the mother or the baby.
why: For questions about the baby's development or the placenta, and for the mother's illnesses when an exact exam is needed.
duration: usually 20 to 45 minutes, the report in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: How far along your pregnancy is
If you have a pacemaker or metal in your body
If you are afraid of closed spaces
If it is hard to lie on your back for long

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: An MRI is usually done after the first trimester, unless there are urgent reasons. The doctor decides.

prepare.title: Contrast
prepare.text: Contrast is usually not given in pregnancy.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no special preparation is needed. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Metal
prepare.text: Take off jewelry, watch and hairpins.

steps: You change clothes and remove metal
You lie on the table on your back or on your side - whichever is comfortable
A light coil is placed on your belly
The table slides into the scanner and you are given earphones
You lie still while the pictures are taken
If you feel unwell, press the call button
feel: Lying on your back you may feel dizzy - say so, and you will be turned on your side
after: You can go home right away
The report is usually ready in 1 to 3 days
Discuss the result with your own doctor

faq.q: Is MRI safe for the baby?
faq.a: MRI does not use radiation. Doctors do it in pregnancy when it is really needed.

faq.q: Will the noise harm the baby's hearing?
faq.a: This has not been shown. Talk about any doubts with your doctor.

reminders.text: MRI tomorrow. Take your pregnancy record and ultrasounds. Take off jewelry before you leave.
